angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,933,350 km at 34.28 pc = 0.75 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75695: distance 34.282 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.026), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 34.282 +/- 0.891 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 27.9256 +/- 0.9703 mas (same row, RUWE 7.30), 28.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 2.779 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75695: radius 2.779 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 29.098 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.867) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 1,933,350 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8047 +/- 3771 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75695: effective temperature 8047 +/- 3771 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75695: effective temperature 8047 +/- 3771 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 137909) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
